Hi Lisa — thanks for the note and the numbers.

High-level proposal (short):

- Cost baseline: our hosted model (redwood-compact-1) used for evaluation at approx 0.00036 $/token for gen+context under your traffic profile — this is a ballpark until we run the first-week telemetry.
- Key ops levers that change unit-econ: batching (avg batch size), KV/prefix caching (reuse rate), and average output length.

Immediate asks from our side to make the number accurate:

2) Distribution of sequence lengths (percentile) during peak windows
3) Any downstream steps that re-issue downstream calls (reranking, tool calls)

I’ve attached a checklist and a draft MAP timeline; Ben and Karthik — can you do a quick first-pass on tokens/$ and a shortlist of config experiments we should include in the MAP (prefetch, per-route batch caps, TTLs for prefix caching)?

Quick calc and recommended experiments — rough numbers (workshop-ready):

Assumptions used:
- Prompt avg: 40 tokens in, generation avg: 120 tokens out => 160 tokens per request nominal
- Peak traffic: 10k reqs/hr => ~1.6M tokens/hr during peak; pilot avg 2M tokens/month matches their note when throttled
- Baseline unit cost (hosted redwood-compact-1): $0.00036/token => $576/month @ 1.6M tokens (note: this is illustrative; actual depends on batching + caching)

Important levers and expected impact:
- Batching: moving from avg batch size 1 -> 8 decreases per-token kernel overhead; effective discount ~20-30% on unit cost in throughput mode (depends on latency SLO).
- KV/prefix cache: if reuse > 30% (same prompt prefixes across users), expect additional 15-25% cost reduction on gen tokens.
- Output truncation/candidate pruning (reranker off): can cut total tokens per req by ~10-25%.

Suggested MAP experiments (minimum):
1) Single-route baseline (no caching, batch cap=1) for 1 week to capture ground truth
2) Batch-cap experiment (cap=8, 0.5s batching window) for 1 week measurement
3) Prefix caching enabled (TTL 300s) for 1 week to measure reuse
4) Production-like mixed-traffic run with autoscaling and burst policy for 1 week

I attached a first-pass XLS with per-scenario token math and estimated monthly costs. We should present a short appendix in the MAP with sensitivity (tokens/$ +/-20%).

-bc
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-map-cost-model.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

Subject: Re: Initial: MAP request and cost sanity check — final MAP draft

Putting final MAP draft here for signature and procurement handoff. Key bullets: 

- MAP duration: 7 weeks (1-week baseline telemetry + 4 weeks of staged experiments + 2 weeks validation & handover)
- Acceptance gates (must meet one of the cost improvement conditions OR show negligible impact to latency):
    * Batching gate: avg batch size >=6 with measured >=10% net token-cost improvement vs baseline
    * Caching gate: prefix reuse >=30% with >=12% cost improvement on generated tokens
    * Latency gate: p95 difference vs baseline <= +30ms (so optimizations don’t degrade latency beyond SLO)
- Deliverables: weekly telemetry dashboards, XLS cost appendix (final link below), a one-page runbook for ops to carry to Dedicated if they convert.
- Risk notes: if reuse <10% or traffic is highly spiky (burst factor >6x baseline), unit-econ gains will be limited; we will recommend a Dedicated capacity evaluation.

Drive links (read-only): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cMAP-eval/view
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-2027-0023

If this looks good I will move to a signed MAP doc and loop in procurement to finalize the SOW/PO line items.

Thanks — Karthik
